l4_usability.notes: 156 lines visible, 21 operator groups. No filter UI exists. Users must scroll to find specific operator.

l5_interaction.notes: Card click opens modal correctly. But no way to filter by operator - user must scroll through 21 groups. CSS for filter bar exists but is never rendered.

l6_adaptation.notes: PC: 21 operator groups, 156 cards. Mobile: no h-scroll. Cards render correctly.

l7_consistency.notes: Same nav, same i18n, same modal pattern as other pages.

l8_industry.notes: Japanese traffic apps typically show operator filters. 156 lines without filtering requires scrolling. Grouped by operator IS implicit filtering.

l9_product.notes: Core functionality works. But finding specific line among 156 requires scrolling through 21 operator groups. Filter UI was designed (CSS exists) but never implemented.

architecture_note: CSS (.rs-filter-bar, .rs-filter-btn) was added in fd025f6 (Task 3.28.2) with description operator filter but JS/HTML never implemented the actual filter buttons. This is dead CSS.

issues_found.root_cause: CSS for operator filter bar exists but JS never renders filter buttons. 156 lines across 21 operators require scrolling without filtering.
issues_found.impact: Users cannot quickly find specific operator lines
issues_found.fix: Add operator filter bar to realtime.html and implement filter logic in realtime-view.js

verdict: P2 CONFIRMED - Filter CSS exists but UI not implemented. Recommend implementing operator filter in 3.60.
